text:
olivia: starting thread — ACME promo workload planning. they warned about sudden spikes during marketing blasts, ~750 rps for 10-15 minutes, baseline ~250 rps. want guidance on reserved vs burst + safe autoscale settings.

devin: key Qs: 1) typical request token length? 2) do they need strict p99 SLA? 3) what model family are they planning to use (13B quant vs 70B fp16)?

olivia: they reported median ~180 tokens, occasional long sessions up to 1500 tokens. target is p95 < 900ms, p50 < 180ms. model: prefer cost-efficient 13B quant but open to fallback.

harpreet: quick throughput calc: 750 rps * 180 tok = 135k tok/s. with 13B quant we get ~1400 tok/s per GPU under our perf profile => ~100 GPUs? wait that math seems off. re-evaluating: if a single GPU handles 1400 tok/s, need ~96 GPUs which is unrealistic. we need to instead rely on batching and KV caching to reduce token work.

devin: agreed, large discrepancy. practical approach: size reserved for steady 250 rps (baseline) and provide burst pool sized in GPU-equivalents to cover ~500 rps additional with fast ramp and prefix cache to slash work. propose reserved 6 GPUs steady and burst capacity equivalent of 6 more GPUs.

lee: operational constraints: preheat KV cache before promo (10m), set burst windows limit (max 20min continuous), and define queue depth throttles to avoid unbounded queuing if autoscale underperforms. also recommend circuit breaker to prefer cached embeddings for repeat queries.

infra-bot: autoscale policy suggestion pasted: ```json
{"min_replicas":"4","max_replicas":"14","scale_metric":"rps","target_rps_per_replica":"80","ramp_cooldown_s":"30"}
```

harpreet: routing strategy: default to quantized 13B. If queue length > 60 requests or replica CPU > 70%, shift a small percent of traffic to fp16 70B until latency stabilizes. this gives graceful degradation path.

devin: pricing note for customer: reserved monthly commit (12mo) + burst credits. reserved lowers per-token by roughly 18-25% depending on quantization. we should ask finance for exact SKU calc.

olivia: security question from ACME: must use customer KMS, need SOC2-level audit logs and option for VPC peering.

sec-bot: checklist: KMS support = yes (Dedicated & Private), Hosted supports envelope encryption + logs export. VPC peering possible in Private. include audit-sample export in appendix.

lee: about queueing behavior: recommend edge rate limiter returning HTTP 429 with Retry-After and a short fallback message for non-critical requests. include client-side retry guidance (exponential backoff, max 3 retries).

harpreet: preflight POC plan: 1) run synthetic load test matching promo profile 2) KV warmup 3) verify autoscale ramp 4) failover to fallback model 5) validate end-to-end KMS + audit log flow. propose 2-hour window for smoke + one-hour promo simulation.

devin: add operational parameters to the proposal: - reserved GPUs: 6 (steady) - burst credits: cover up to additional 500 rps for 15m windows - autoscale: min 4 / max 14 (fast ramp) - preheat: 10m @200 rps - fallback: quant13 -> fp1670 when latency trigger hit

olivia: can someone draft the POC runbook and a short appendix with expected latency vs cost curves for the two models? include a tiny example of the autoscale JSON and a sketch of KV preheat command.

lee: i'll draft runbook. KV preheat example (curl):
```bash
for i in $(seq 1 1200); do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/preheat -d '{"prefix":"promo-abc","hits":1}' & done
```

harpreet: also include guidance on monitoring alerts: p95 latency > 1s, queue depth > 100, replica error rate > 1% -> trigger paging and fallback.

devin: final: schedule a 30-min preflight with ACME ops tomorrow. olivia to confirm time. I'll contact finance for 12mo reserved quote + burst addon.

olivia: confirming now. thanks all — will assemble proposal: reserved 6 GPUs, burst capacity for +500 rps, autoscale min4/max14, KV preheat, routing fallback, security appendix. draft by EOD. :white_check_mark:
